name: Summit at Granby Apartments
award: 2024 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Summit Housing Group's Summit at Granby Apartments is a 67-unit modular new-construction family project (66 income-restricted at 30% to 80% AMI plus one employee unit) on Pioneer Drive in Granby, pitched as the town's first housing tax credit development; it won 2024 Round Two federal 4% and accelerated state credits from CHFA, with $16.82M of CHFA bonds.
why_it_matters: Nearly two years after the award the project is still in Granby's final plat and site plan review, its original modular builder is in arbitration seeking $5.7M, and the neighboring HOA is contesting dues and road terms, so practitioners should treat it as at risk of further delay.

status.label: Credits awarded; land bought; town approvals still pending as of May 2026; no construction start found
status.detail: Summit bought the site in February 2025. The town deemed its final plat and plan application complete on 2026-04-28 and issued review comments on 2026-05-12, targeting a 2026-07-06 Planning Commission hearing and a 2026-07-28 Board of Trustees date; no record of those hearings, a building permit, a bond closing or groundbreaking was found. Sky-Hi News (March 2026) showed the site as an empty lot and reported that modular builder Fading West had been ordered to stop work and is seeking $5.7M in arbitration.

next_step: Watch Granby Planning Commission and Board of Trustees agendas for the final plat and plan, the parking adjustment, and any HOA agreement, then a CHFA bond closing and building permit.

key_numbers.meaning: 6 studios, 16 one-bedroom, 37 two-bedroom and 7 three-bedroom units at 30% to 80% AMI (average 60%), plus one employee unit.
About $15.1M over 10 years, plus $764,007 of accelerated state credit (the applicant had asked for $1,424,472 of state credit).
Privately placed with Bellwether Enterprise per the application, which proposed $17.5M ($8.04M permanent, $9.48M short-term construction).
About $472,000 per unit in the application, reflecting mountain construction costs.

facts.value: 23 Pioneer Drive, Granby 80446 (deed also lists 15 Pioneer Drive and 12 and 16 Morris Drive); Lots 1, 2, 7 and 8, Block 4, Silvercreek West First Addition, replatted as Amended Lot 1
About 2.93 acres; zoned HGB (Highway General Business) within Silvercreek West PDOD #5-2002, where multifamily is allowed by right

Two-story modular buildings on crawlspace foundations with interior hallways, hail-resistant roof and solar for common areas; 2026 plans show a north and a west building ("Granby Alt-Mod" plans by EVstudio)
135 spaces required; 33 proposed as compact, which needs a Board of Trustees parking adjustment
Enterprise Green Communities; all-electric design with photovoltaic system per CHFA; heat-pump washer/dryers; EV charging
Free Granby-Winter Park bus stop about 0.4 mile away; Amtrak station under half a mile
Fraser River Valley Housing Partnership to be special limited partner, giving property tax abatement (about $23,000 per unit in value per the applicant)
Capture rate 14.9%; zero vacancy and a waitlist at the one LIHTC property in the market area
Phase I (March 2025 report for 15 and 23 Pioneer Drive) posted by the town; the application says the Phase I found no recognized environmental conditions

background.text: Summit first pitched a 45-unit, 30% to 60% AMI project on two Pioneer Drive lots; Granby trustees voted support on 2023-01-24 and the Fraser River Valley Housing Partnership on 2023-01-23. It then applied for competitive 9% credits in 2023 and in 2024 Round One (50 units, 49 low-income, $1,450,000 requested) without an award, before growing to 67 units with income averaging in the 4% round.
The Granby Board of Trustees took up a Summit Housing Group proposal on 2024-01-09 and a Summit at Granby letter of support on 2024-08-13.
Summit bought Lots 1, 2, 7 and 8, Block 4, Silvercreek West First Addition from JJBJ LLC for $1,700,000 by warranty deed dated 2025-02-26, recorded 2025-02-28 at reception no. 2025001842.

A town site plan review dated 2025-07-29 describes 68 residential units plus an office and a community room; the civil engineer's application (dated 2025-08-06) targeted Planning Commission approval on 2025-09-09 and grading in fall 2025, which did not happen on that schedule.

Fading West, the Buena Vista modular maker picked in 2023 under a $10.2M agreement, is seeking $5.7M from Summit in arbitration after Summit ordered it to stop work; 2026 building plans by EVstudio carry the title "Granby Alt-Mod", suggesting an alternate modular design (inferred).

In a 2026-03-09 letter Summit told the Silvercreek homeowners association that its LIHTC financing cannot carry HOA dues or widening Pioneer Drive beyond 24 feet and offered about $8,000 a year toward road maintenance; the HOA's 2026-05-08 response to the town says the project lacks its architectural approval and that dues are required.

The town deemed the final plat and plan application complete on 2026-04-28; review comments came from CDOT, East Grand School District, Granby Sanitation District, the HOA, Mountain Parks Electric and Xcel Energy.

Summit and its affiliates report LIHTC housing in Colorado, Montana, Wyoming, South Dakota, Utah and Idaho, including Academy Place in Broomfield; the project does not serve special-needs populations and no project-based vouchers are described.

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists 67 units, the town's July 2025 site plan review describes 68 residential units, and the March 2026 Sky-Hi News story describes a 76-unit project.
CHFA, the deed and the town documents give the address as 23 Pioneer Drive, while Sky-Hi News gives 24 Pioneer Drive.
The award report lists $16,820,000 in bonds, while the application proposed $17,525,754.
CHFA awarded $764,007 of state credit, while the applicant requested $1,424,472 and its capital stack assumed $6,296,492 of state credit equity.
The application dates the Fraser River Valley housing needs assessment to August 2024 in one place and August 2022 in another.

open_questions: Whether the Planning Commission and trustees approved the final plat, site plan and parking adjustment in July 2026, and whether the HOA dispute was settled.
Who will build the modular units now that Fading West was stopped, and the outcome of its arbitration claim.
Whether the CHFA bonds have closed and a building permit has been issued; the March 2025 start target has long passed.
How the smaller state credit award ($764,007 versus $1.42M requested) was filled, and whether the DOLA money was awarded.
Rents, CHFA affordability period and current total development cost.
